skill_traces.query:
Evan: Hey Sam, what's up? Long time no see, huh? Lots has happened.
Sam: Hey Evan! Long time no see. I'm doing okay, been through a few bumps. How about you?
Evan: It's not easy for us right now, my son had an accident last Tuesday, he fell off his bike and it was rough. But he's doing better now. How are you dealing with all this?
Sam: Darn, sorry to hear that. Hope he's feeling better. Same here, it's been tough lately. After we talked, I started thinking about ways to cope with it, but it's been challenging.
Evan: Life can be hard sometimes. Do you have any hobbies or activities that make you happy?
Sam: I used to love hiking, but it's been a while since I had the chance to do it.
Evan: I remember you mentioning that! Hiking is indeed a great way to center oneself and be one with nature. We should definitely plan a hike soon!
Sam: Yeah, I'm struggling with my weight and it's affecting my confidence. I feel like I can't overcome all the challenges with my weight, I keep lacking motivation.
Evan: Yeah, I understand it can be challenging. But remember, it's important to believe in yourself and take it one day at a time, Sam. Your worth is not defined by your weight.
Sam: Cheers, Evan. Appreciate the help. It's tough breaking out of my comfort zone.
Evan: Stepping out of your comfort zone can be intimidating, but it's totally worth it. Just challenge yourself to try something new, even if it's just a little thing. You got this!
Sam: Thanks, Evan. I'll take your advice. Trying new things can be difficult.
Evan: Yeah, trying something new and succeeding gives a great feeling of accomplishment. Give it a go, even if it's just a little thing. You'll be amazed!
Sam: She looks so confident! What kind of painting is that in the background?
Evan: 
This is a contemporary figurative painting that I've finished few days ago, emphasizing the emotional state through expressive brushwork and vibrant color choices. It captures a moment of introspection, where the subject is deeply immersed in thought. Very proud of it!
Sam: That's amazing work, who's the girl standing next to painting?
Evan: That's a close friend of mine who helped me get this painting published in the exhibition!

selected.name: Extract Behavior-Purpose Links
selected.description: Use when a speaker explicitly connects an activity or behavior to a purpose like stress relief, comfort, boredom, or motivation.
content: During extraction, if a speaker links a behavior (eating, exercise, visiting a place, etc.) to a purpose or internal state (stress relief, comfort, motivation), create a memory candidate that records the behavior as a means to that purpose, using memory kind 'preference' or 'event' as appropriate.
Do not let a concurrent emotional state (e.g., guilt) replace this behavior-purpose fact.

During CRUD, when such a preference candidate is present, do not merge or overwrite it with a broader state memory that omits the purpose; preserve the behavior-purpose link unless new evidence contradicts it.
selected.rerank_reason: Sam mentions struggling with weight and lacking motivation, which is linked to a behavior (struggling with weight) and an internal state (lack of motivation). This directly connects a behavior to a purpose or internal state, making the skill applicable.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Claims from Figurative Language
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message contains figurative, exclamatory, or metaphorical language that ascribes an attribute or feeling to a subject.
content: During candidate extraction, do not skip expressive or figurative statements as non-factual.

If a speaker uses exclamatory or metaphorical phrasing (e.g., 'it's magical', 'pure bliss', 'a nightmare') to describe their feeling about an activity, person, or object, create a `preference` or `profile` candidate that captures the literal attribute or opinion stated.
Preserve the compared object or image verbatim or as a close paraphrase within the memory content; extract only the explicit claim, do not infer additional attributes.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Offers, Encouragement, and Advice
nearby_not_selected.description: Use during extraction when a message contains one person offering help, giving advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
content: During extraction, treat a single message as sufficient evidence when a speaker offers help, gives advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
Create one event memory capturing the speaker, the recipient, and the gist of what was said, including any explicit guidance or offer topic.
Stop after the gist is captured; do not infer the recipient's internal feelings or expand into multiple memory kinds unless the message contains other distinct facts.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Photo-Sharing Events
nearby_not_selected.description: When a message presents an object or result with visual language like 'Here are...' or explicitly mentions sharing a photo, during extraction.
content: When a message uses presentation phrasing such as 'Here are...', 'Check out...', 'This is a photo of...', or 'Attached is...' to introduce something, record that the speaker shared a photo of that item, even if the word 'photo' does not appear.

If the speaker explicitly mentions sharing, sending, or showing a picture/photo/image, create an event memory that records the sharing action and the described content (e.g., subject or creator of the picture).
Preserve the literal object named in the message (e.g., picture) — do not replace it with an inferred object such as a bookshelf, item, or possession.
Keep the sharing act within the same event memory as the other facts from that message; do not summarize away the visual sharing.
Only include facts explicitly stated; do not convert a shared picture into an ownership claim unless ownership is directly stated.
